newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Madrid confirmed for NATO enlargement summit.
newsitem.headline: Madrid confirmed for NATO enlargement summit.

text.p: NATO foreign ministers have agreed on Madrid as the venue for a summit on July 8-9 next year to set the course for enlargement of the alliance, a NATO official said on Tuesday.
"It is going to be Madrid," the official told Reuters.
At the summit, NATO intends to invite a number of former communist foes to begin membership talks. Hungary, Poland and the Czech republic are considered the most likely.

Earlier, NATO Secretary General Javier Solana, a former Spanish foreign minister, told the allies the summit would "shape the new NATO -- a NATO with new structures, new missions and ultimately with new members."
"Next year's summit will mark the moment when the processes of tranformation and change converge as the new alliance takes stock," he said.

The alliance also has to discuss what to offer to eastern hopefuls who are thought unlikely to be in the first enlargement wave -- notably the Baltic states, Bulgaria and Slovakia and how to sweeten expansion for a deeply opposed Russia.
